result_expr: 3*gamma*eps*(Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), x)**2 + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), y)**2 + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), z)**2) + 3*gamma/eps*phi(x, y, z, t)**2*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))**2

symbols.name: W
symbols.meaning: height scale of the double-well potential

symbols.name: xi
symbols.meaning: coordinate normal to a flat interface, with the interface at xi = 0

symbols.name: phi_0
symbols.meaning: equilibrium profile across a flat interface

steps.title: Ansatz for the free energy density
steps.why: The density is a double well, which makes $\phi=0$ and $\phi=1$ the only stable uniform states. The wells have equal depth because the temperature is at coexistence (A1), so there is no tilt term. A gradient term penalizes sharp changes in $\phi$, which gives the interface a finite width and a positive energy.

check.printed: no tools in this run; units: $\kappa|\nabla\phi|^2$ has J m^-1 m^-2 = J m^-3, and $W$ has J m^-3

steps.title: First integral for a flat interface
steps.why: For a flat interface, $\phi$ depends only on $\xi$. The Euler-Lagrange equation $\kappa\phi''=W\,d[\phi^2(1-\phi)^2]/d\phi$ has a first integral. Its constant is zero because $\phi'\to0$ and the well term vanishes in both bulk phases.
steps.operation: multiply the Euler-Lagrange equation by $\phi'$ and integrate once in $\xi$

steps.title: Equilibrium profile
steps.why: Take the root with ice at $\xi\to-\infty$ and gas at $\xi\to+\infty$, then separate variables.
steps.operation: take the square root and integrate

check.printed: no tools in this run; by hand, $\phi_0'=-\sqrt{2W/\kappa}\,\phi_0(1-\phi_0)$ holds

steps.title: Interface energy
steps.why: The excess energy per unit area is the integral of $f$ across the interface. By S2 the two terms are equal, so it equals $\int\kappa\phi_0'^2\,d\xi$. Changing the variable to $\phi$ gives a closed form.
steps.operation: integrate over $\xi$ and change the variable to $\phi$

steps.title: Fix the length scale
steps.why: Define $\varepsilon$ as the decay length of the profile's tails, $\phi_0\sim e^{-|\xi|/\varepsilon}$. This sets $\sqrt{2W/\kappa}=1/\varepsilon$. The width is $\delta=1/|\phi_0'(0)|=4\varepsilon$; the 10-90% width is $2\ln 9\,\varepsilon$.

steps.title: Solve for the coefficients
steps.why: Multiplying and dividing S4 and S5 gives $2W=6\gamma/\varepsilon$ and $2/\kappa=1/(3\gamma\varepsilon)$.

check.printed: no tools in this run; check: $\sqrt{2\cdot3\gamma/\varepsilon\cdot6\gamma\varepsilon}/6=\gamma$
no tools in this run; units: J m^-2 m m^-2 = J m^-3, and J m^-2 m^-1 = J m^-3

assumptions_used: A1: the temperature is uniform and constant, at phase coexistence, so the bulk ice and bulk gas free energies are equal and the double well is symmetric.
A2: the interface energy $\gamma$ is isotropic, and the free energy is local, depending on $\phi$ and $\nabla\phi$ only (square-gradient approximation).
A3: the width scale $\varepsilon$ is defined by the tail decay $\phi_0\sim e^{-|\xi|/\varepsilon}$, which gives the reported width $\delta=1/|\phi_0'(0)|=4\varepsilon$.

neglected.why: By A1 the system is at coexistence; this would add a tilt term such as $\propto\phi^2(3-2\phi)$.
They are not part of this functional at coexistence; they couple in only away from equilibrium.

neglected.effect: Anisotropy of the ice surface energy
neglected.why: $\gamma$ is taken to be constant, as stated.

neglected.effect: Contact with the regolith grains (wetting, grain surface energies)
neglected.why: The pore space is treated as ice plus gas only; boundary terms would add surface integrals.
These are higher order in $\varepsilon$ over the feature size, and second derivatives are excluded by the work order.

questions: The coefficients depend on how $\varepsilon$ is tied to the width. I used the tail decay length, giving $\tanh(\xi/2\varepsilon)$ and $\delta=4\varepsilon$. If the project uses $\tanh(\xi/\varepsilon)$ instead, the result becomes $f=\tfrac32\gamma\varepsilon|\nabla\phi|^2+\tfrac{6\gamma}{\varepsilon}\phi^2(1-\phi)^2$. Please confirm the convention.
